sentences.text: 19. Final arguments addressed by the Ld. APP for State and Ld.
Counsel for accused were heard and case file was perused.
20. It is argued by Ld. counsel for the accused that complainant has not been examined in the case.
The signature of complainant is not consistent as per the FSL report and therefore, opinion on her signature was not given.
LIC policy without photographs are not admissible.
No monetary benefit is received by the accused in the case.
All the amount goes to the account of agent.
The principal has not disputed the signature and school seal.
He did not bring the original documents attested copy.
Merely attested copy were produced by him.
It is also not proved that the Indian Passport was surrendered by the complainant or not.
Thus, prosecution has failed to prove its case.
21. Before proceeding with the appreciation of evidence, I shall deal with the relevant laws involved in the case.
Section 420 Indian Penal Code deals with Cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property.

The provision reads as - "Whoever cheats and thereby dishonestly induces the person deceived to deliver any property to any person, or to make, State Vs. Ashwani Kumar FIR No. : 810/2014 PS Hauz Khas U/s 120B and 420/467 IPC Page no.12 of 18 alter or destroy the whole or any part of a valuable security, or anything which is signed or sealed, and which is capable of being converted into a valuable security, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine."
22. Forgery is defined under Section 463 of Indian Penal Code. The section reads as "Whosoever makes any fake document or incorrect electronic record or part of a document with an intention to cause damage or injury, to the public or to any person, or to support any claim or title, or to cause any person to share with property, or to enter into any express or implied contract, or with purpose to commit fraud or that fraud may be accomplished, commits forgery."

sentences.text: In order to constitute forgery, the first essential is that- a. the accused should have made a false document.
b. And secondly, the false document must be made with an intention to cause harm or injury to the public or to any class of society or to any community.
23. 'False document' is dealt under section 464 IPC.
The definition of "false document" is a part of the definition of State Vs. Ashwani Kumar FIR No. : 810/2014 PS Hauz Khas U/s 120B and 420/467 IPC Page no.13 of 18 "forgery".

entities.text: State Vs. Ashwani Kumar FIR No. : 810/2014
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Both must be read together.

An analysis of section 464 of Indian Penal Code shows that it divides false documents into three categories:
1) The first is where a person dishonestly or fraudulently makes or executes a document with the intention of causing it to be believed that such document was made or executed by some other person, or by the authority of some other person, by whom or by whose authority he knows it was not made or executed.
2) The second is where a person dishonestly or fraudulently, by cancellation or otherwise, alters a document in any material part, without lawful authority, after it has been made or executed by either himself or any other person.

3) The third is where a person dishonestly or fraudulently causes any person to sign,
execute or alter a document knowing that such person could not by reason of (a)
unsoundness of mind; or (b) intoxication; or (c) deception practised upon him, know the contents of the document or the nature of the alteration.
24. Section 467 IPC provides punishment for 'forgery of valuable security, Will etc'.

As per the Section 'Whoever forges a document which purports to be a valuable security or a will, or an authority to adopt a son, or which purports to give authority to any State Vs. Ashwani Kumar FIR No. : 810/2014 PS Hauz Khas U/s 120B and 420/467 IPC Page no.14 of 18 person to make or transfer any valuable security, or to receive the principal, interest or dividends thereon, or to receive or deliver any money, movable property, or valuable security, or any document purporting to be an acquittance or receipt acknowledging the payment of money, or an acquittance or receipt for the delivery of any movable property or valuable security, shall be punished with imprisonment for life,
or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine."

sentences.text: It is worth mentioning that though IO had not conducted any investigation regarding the genuineness of signature and stamp of principal affixed on the photocopy of ID card of Sakshi.

In the absence of the original policy document allegedly executed with complainant and also in the absence of testimony of the complainant, it cannot be proved that accused had forged the ID card and documents pertaining to Sakshi and on that basis, they had obtained policy in the name of complainant.
29. PW7 Purushottam Bahl who was the Marketing Officer in the marketing dept. at the time of incident has also not deposed anything against accused.
It is also relevant to state that in the FSL examination conducted in the case no opinion has been expressed on the handwriting of accused Ashwani as the same were found not consistent on comparison.

sentences.text: It is well settled that in a criminal trial the burden of proof is on the prosecution to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt.
Any contradiction or iota of proof in favour of accused can completely dismantle the case of prosecution.

In the present case there are no cogent material on record to suggest accused had committed cheating with complainant by inducing her to obtain the policy documents from Birla Sunlife Insurance Pvt. Ltd. on the false pretext of payment of only one time premium.

It is also not proved in the case that accused had forged the application in the name of complainant for reconsideration of refund cheque for issuing policy in the name of her grand daughter (fictitious person as Sakshi) for claiming any incentive by accused.
Considering the entire circumstances of the case, allegations against accused are not proved in the case.
Conclusion & Decision 31.
Considering the above discussion and material placed on record, I hold that the prosecution had failed prove its case against the accused beyond reasonable doubts.
Accused Ashwani Kumar S/o Chattar Singh is accordingly acquitted of offence u/s 120B IPC & 420/467 IPC.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
He never had the direct contact with the customers.
The agents used to bring the customers and he only help the customers in filing the proposal forms.
He used to fill the proposal forms by himself in normal course of business as being directed by the Insurance Company since the columns in the same contains the technical language and to prevent the customers from harassment at the time of claim.
Sometimes he used to help them and sometime he used to fill their form and then they got it signed by the customers through their respective agents.
Moreover, he never get any monetary benefit by issuing any insurance policy.
18. Accused did not lead defence evidence.
The principal has not disputed the signature and school seal.
He did not bring the original documents attested copy.
Merely attested copy were produced by him.
It is also not proved that the Indian Passport was surrendered by the complainant or not.
Thus, prosecution has failed to prove its case.
State vs Ashwini Kumar Etc (20 on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138771250/
6
In order to constitute forgery, the first essential is that- a. the accused should have made a false document.
b. And secondly, the false document must be made with an intention to cause harm or injury to the public or to any class of society or to any community.
The definition of "false document" is a part of the definition of State Vs. Ashwani Kumar FIR No. : 810/2014 PS Hauz Khas U/s 120B and 420/467 IPC Page no.13 of 18 "forgery".
Both must be read together.
This fact also does not prove that accused promised the complainant or induced her to believe that only one time premium is required to be paid by her and on that pretext, he had got signed the LIC policy from her.
None had appeared on their behalf along with the original insurance policy.
IN the absence of original insurance policy on record, merely on the basis of secondary evidence, the insurance policy with the complainant cannot be relied upon for placing reliance upon the case.
It is well settled that in a criminal trial the burden of proof is on the prosecution to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt.
Any contradiction or iota of proof in favour of accused can completely dismantle the case of prosecution.
In the present case there are no cogent material on record to suggest accused had committed cheating with complainant by inducing her to obtain the policy documents from Birla Sunlife Insurance Pvt. Ltd. on the false pretext of payment of only one time premium.
It is also not proved in the case that accused had forged the application in the name of complainant for reconsideration of refund cheque for issuing policy in the name of her grand daughter (fictitious person as Sakshi) for claiming any incentive by accused.
Considering the entire circumstances of the case, allegations against accused are not proved in the case.
Considering the above discussion and material placed on record, I hold that the prosecution had failed prove its case against the accused beyond reasonable doubts.
